category_title: Students with limited expressive language who use visual supports and exhibit avoidance behaviors
minimal_context: Evan is being asked to transition to a one-on-one work area to complete two-digit addition and subtraction problems.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Evan, it is time for our 30-minute work time. Let's move to the work area to write the answers to your five addition and five subtraction problems.

STUDENT: (Evan does not follow the direction. He stands in place, flipping a straw back and forth in front of his eyes.)

TUTOR: Evan, please put the straw down and come over to the table.

STUDENT: (Evan drops to the floor and lies down instead of moving to the structured task area.)

TUTOR: You need to get up now so we can finish your math work.

STUDENT: (Evan crawls under the table to avoid the work. When approached, he protests the activity by kicking at the adult.)

options.A: Use a visual schedule that identifies activities of the day and the reinforcers the student is eligible to receive for contingent performance.
options.B: Avoid placing time pressure on the student; allow him to work at his own pace to make sense of the addition and subtraction problems.
options.C: Maintain a quiet and relaxing environment in the one-on-one work area; talk gently and slowly; avoid loud speech during the session.
options.D: Use basketball, popular music, or skateboarding references to engage the student in the addition and subtraction problems during the one-on-one work time.
